idea.en: Find the heart through the liver from the subxiphoid.

alt.en: Echo Lab render of the Subcostal four chamber. Press flat under the xiphoid and hang the heart below the liver.

caption.en: Echo Lab render of the Subcostal four chamber. Press flat under the xiphoid and hang the heart below the liver.

note.en: Landmarks to confirm: Cavity of left ventricle

steps.en: What you see: The liver caps the top of the image and the heart hangs below it with all four chambers in a near field close up. The septa run across the screen and fluid, when present, rims the heart in black.
Landmarks to confirm: Do not accept the view until each of these is on screen.
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Each mistake below comes from the view catalogue with its correction.
Normal values and effusion method: Left ventricular ejection fraction 55 percent or more is normal, below 30 percent is severely reduced.
Report the largest diastolic echo free space in millimetres and name where it sits.
Tamponade is physiology not size, so report right atrial and right ventricular collapse with respiration.

Pitfalls: Fat looks like fluid but moves with the wall, while fluid stays outside it; epicardial fat sits in front of the right ventricle. In trauma, blood also collects in Morison pouch, so a cardiac look alone never clears the abdomen.
Indian context: In India think of tuberculosis behind a large fibrinous effusion with thick strands, and of rheumatic disease when an effusion comes with mitral stenosis.

analogy.en: Landmarks to confirm: Cavity of left ventricle

spot.en: Landmarks to confirm: Cavity of left ventricle
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Liver too dark from bowel gas so the heart drops out. Correct it by pressing firmer under the costal margin and trying again after a breath out.
Plane too anterior showing only the right heart. Correct it by angling more posteriorly until the left chambers open beside the right.
Foreshortened septum from a cranial probe position. Correct it by flattening the probe further and sliding slightly down.

todo.en: How to get it: Place the probe at subxiphoid, pressed flat under the costal margin.
Point the probe marker toward the left, about three o clock.
Press the probe flat under the xiphoid, almost horizontal, and ask the patient to bend the knees. If bowel gas blocks, press a little firmer and wait for the gas to shift.
Freeze the image only when every listed landmark is on screen at once.

q.en: How should the probe sit for the subcostal four chamber?

o.en: Flat under the xiphoid, almost horizontal

why.en: A flat subxiphoid probe looks up through the liver at the heart.

q.en: Bright tissue in front of the right ventricle moves with the wall. What is it?

why.en: Fat moves with the wall while fluid stays outside it.

q.en: A large effusion shows right atrial collapse in late diastole with right ventricular collapse in early diastole, a dilated cava and hypotension. What does this mean?

o.en: Tamponade physiology needing immediate senior review for drainage

why.en: Late diastolic atrial collapse with early diastolic ventricular collapse plus a dilated cava and hypotension means tamponade physiology, so arrange immediate senior review for drainage.
